My overall goal in life is the cultivation of a Post-Industrial culture in order to rescue the environment and society from the now pathological paradigms of a slowly failing Industrial Age. 'Post-Industrial' does not mean anti-industrial nor does it relate to the misappropriation of the term by economists using it to refer to western nations that have off-loaded industrial production to the developing world. Rather, it refers, in a general sense, to whatever comes after the Industrial Age and which has not yet become named as definitive of the era, as we usually only recognize these things after the fact. Futurist Alvin Toffler referred to this as the Third Wave, the first being the Agrarian era and the second the Industrial era. Some have suggested the so-called Information, Computer, or Digital Age but these technologies have not altered the essential paradigms on which the culture is founded, only amplified their effects. Toffler suggested the key feature of the Third Wave was a trend of technologically facilitated demassification; the reversing of the Industrial Age's trend of massification deriving from the mass production paradigm. Technologies of independent power, production, and communications. The creation of new 'commons' as with open source technology and cryptocurrency. I add to this the trend of increasingly peer-oriented and/or stigmergic organization as well as the emergence of Social Capital systems, thus we may eventually, in hindsight, refer to a Social Age, a Stigmergic Age, or a Cybernetic Age.

In any case, I am very passionate about developing and distributing technology that empowers society through industrial independence and digitally enhanced social networking/organization. New decentralized technologies for communication, organization, and exchange that can whittle-away at our monolithic and hierarchical power structures. New building/housing technology that enables the solitary owner-builder and reduces the dependence on mortgages while improving the environmental sustainability of our lifestyles. New farming technology that facilitates food security through localization of production. Independent open industrial technology like the new digital fabrication tools that whittle-away at our dependence on the market and, subsequently, corporate salaries. And, yes, even technologies like space telerobotics facilitating open public access to space development. I like to imagine myself as the 21st Century high-tech equivalent of Dr. Lao.
